clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms: exempts the employee 'until September 1, 1935'. Recorded as 1935-09-01, inclusive; exclusive alternative stated in the rationale.

research_rationale:
Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/(MIRROR_)DOCUMENTS.jsonl has a heading naming this order number, a date and subject agreeing with the held text, and a text_sha256 equal to the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. EO 6825 (August 20, 1934), read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (two held copies of the same page, sha256 shared), exempts C. Frank Wittenauer, picture engraver, Bureau of Engraving and Printing from section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 and continues the employee in the service until September 1, 1935. Identity: number, date, person and title agree across the APP page, the census register and the WPA 1944 numbered list. The order recites EO 6610 of February 21, 1934 (recited earlier exemption; an earlier grant, not an event on this order). Legal reading: a single time-limited grant that ends by its own terms on 1935-09-01, inclusive; the census, WPA and full-text name searches found no later order naming this person, so no extension or earlier end is held. Authority: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), whose proviso lets the President exempt a person from automatic separation at retirement age. No held source shows section 204 repealed or amended before this order's stated end. Held texts of later exemptions show the President still granting exemptions under section 204 after this date (for example EO 7725 of October 1937, under section 204, running to November 1, 1938), which corroborates that the statutory scheme ran through the stated date.

The employee's death or separation before the date would leave the exemption unused but is not, on the order's text, an end of the order, and no held record shows such an event. The date is a fixed term of the grant, not a deadline on some other act.","independent_command_check":"The order contains one operative command, the time-limited exemption of one named employee.
